question: Can parameter tuning of darkspot-v1 reduce the look-alike false-positive rate without costing oil recall?

method.development: train+val, 384 real Sentinel-1 scenes (128 per class)
method.confirmation: test, 66 scenes (22 per class), measured ONCE with a single pre-registered configuration and no sweep
method.split: data/splits/part3-split.json — whole 1.0-degree geographic cells assigned to one split
method.selectionRule: oil detection rate is a hard floor; the objective is the look-alike rate alone; oil mean IoU breaks ties. Recall was deliberately NOT traded off inside a combined score.
laddersSwept: all promising combinations of the last three

chosenOnDevelopment.why: On 384 development scenes it removed 8.5 points of look-alike false positives and 7.8 points of clean-sea false positives at ZERO recall cost — the only gate that reduced false positives without missing a real slick.

decision: NOT ADOPTED — darkspot-v1 keeps its shipped parameters.
rationale: The development gain did not transfer. On the held-out split the look-alike false-positive rate is UNCHANGED at 68.2% (15 of 22 scenes, identical to baseline), while oil IoU falls 0.028. The clean-sea improvement of 4.5 points is exactly one scene out of 22, which is within noise at this sample size. Adopting a configuration that costs segmentation quality and returns nothing measurable on unseen data would be tuning to the development set and calling it progress.
whatThisEstablishes: The look-alike problem is not reachable by thresholds, area gates, shape gates or risk gates on the classical detector. Rungs 1-5 of the 14 Phase 9 ladder are now measured and exhausted.
supportingFinding: The gates are largely REDUNDANT rather than complementary. Adding an elongation gate on top of the risk gate changed the false-positive rate by exactly zero on 384 scenes, because look_alike_risk() already contains an elongation term (r_shape). Tuning them jointly cannot help.
secondFinding: Across every configuration swept, the mean look-alike risk assigned to false positives stayed in the 0.15-0.29 band. No parameter setting makes the detector's own warning channel informative about its own errors — it remains wrong AND unwarned.
next: Rungs 6-7: focal loss to down-weight easy negatives, and a trained look-alike classifier. Look-alike scenes carry no positive pixels, so a segmentation objective alone teaches no rejection — which is also why the U-Net trained earlier scored better on oil IoU and worse on look-alikes.
